subject: Dedicated capacity SKU tiering framework for Solara Health - H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs
messages:
From: Anna Kim <anna.kim@solarahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Torres <mike.torres@solarahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 23:03:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing help - Solara ML profile attached

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a follow-up with our ML infra and procurement teams and they asked for a concrete recommendation for Dedicated SKU selection and a sizing sketch tied to our expected workload. High-level:

- Workload mix: 60% interactive chat (short context, 512-2k tokens, p95 latency target 120-200ms), 30% embeddings/batch offline (large batch throughput), 10% long-context summarization (context up to 64k tokens, lower concurrency but very memory hungry).
- Expected peak concurrency (user-facing): ~350 concurrent small gen requests.
- Batch jobs: daily embedding jobs ~5M texts, prefer cheap units.
- SLOs: 99p latency budget for interactive, cost target: keep per-token cost within our stated procurement band.

Attached is a short profile of current models and sample token mix (Solara_ML_profile.xlsx). We'd like a recommendation that balances latency, memory headroom for KV cache/long context, and cost predictability for a year-long reserved pool. We also need an ops fallback strategy: if primary SKU is exhausted, what should we fall back to?

Could Kimberly or Ben join a call to walk through ops constraints, and do you have a simple tiering matrix we can include with our procurement packet?

Appreciate it,

Anna
VP Engineering, Solara Health
[Attachment: Solara_ML_profile.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@solarahealth.com>

Hi Anna — thanks for the profile and clear constraints. Looping in Kimberly, Ben and Priyom to give a combined recommendations + ops tiering matrix. High-level summary of what we'd propose (quick take, attaching a compact table):

- Tiered SKUs (recommended):
  * L4 pool: serve low-latency, high-concurrency short-context requests (cheap per-token, minimal KV cache requirements).
  * H100 pool: primary for long-context summarization and high-throughput generative workloads that benefit from FP16/FP8 compute density and high memory bandwidth. Best for 64k-token runs and large batches that need >80GB aggregate model memory for KV/cache.
  * A100 pool: memory-first fallback for mid-long context when H100 capacity is constrained, or for models that prefer larger single-GPU memory (40GB/80GB variants).

- Why this split: L4 is most cost-efficient for short responses and embeddings; H100 provides best perf for large-token, compute-bound runs; A100 provides deterministic memory headroom and is an easier fallthrough when H100 is oversubscribed.

- Sample sizing (sketch for reserved pool):
  * L4: 16x L4 nodes, optimized for 512-2k token gen; expected p95 latency ~90-150ms at 350 concurrency with batching + prefix cache.
  * H100: 6x H100 80GB nodes dedicated to long-context and heavy throughput; target for 64k context workloads (KV+model) and high batch throughput windows.
  * A100: 4x A100 80GB nodes as warm failover capacity and for memory-heavy single-GPU tasks.

- Key operational controls:
  * Routing policy: user-facing routes -> L4 cluster. Long-context jobs flagged by header -> H100. If H100 utilization >85% -> route overflow to A100 with graceful model variant (quantized or shorter context) or queue.
  * Cache sizing: reserve ~15-25% memory headroom on H100 for persistent KV cache; quantify KV size per convo using your median context length (we can calc if you share samples).
  * Quantization: recommend FP8 + int8 eval for embeddings/batch workloads on L4/A100; caution with FP8 for RLHF/very long context unless validated.

I've attached a short matrix with cost ballparks and a fallback ladder: dedicated-sku-options-v1.xlsx. Can we set a 45-minute call Wednesday to walk through numbers and a procurement-friendly one-pager?

—Evelyn
Senior Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Anna / team — adding implementation-level constraints and a short checklist you can show procurement.

Implementation notes (practical numbers):
- Model memory and KV estimates:
  * 64k-token long-context on H100: assume ~60-70GB model + 10-25GB KV working set depending on session retention; reserve 20% headroom for OS and runtime -> plan 80GB per long-context slot.
  * A100 80GB carb: good for single-GPU large inference with predictable memory; H100 still better for throughput at similar memory thanks to attention kernel perf.
  * L4: great for 16k-ish contexts and majority of chat interactions with low per-token cost; KV cache smaller (2–6GB).

- Concurrency math (back-of-envelope):
  * Short-gen path (L4): 350 concurrent users -> with efficient batching (avg batch size 4) and prefix cache we estimate ~16 L4 GPUs to sustain p95 120–180ms. If you plan aggressive caching, you can drop to ~12 nodes.
  * Long-context path (H100): concurrency 8–16 parallel long-context runs during peak; 6 H100s with slotting/tiling handles this with headroom if you limit maximum parallel 64k runs to ~12 concurrently.

- Fallback/tiling behavior:
  * When H100 utilization is high: tile large requests across multiple A100s is possible but increases latency and complexity; prefer a graceful degrade policy: shorten max context (e.g., 64k -> 32k) or serve a condensed summary + background re-run on A100 spot.
  * For embeddings: run on L4 in quantized int8 to reduce cost; move to A100/H100 only if memory or model variant requires it.

- Ops checklist for procurement packet:
  * SLA options by pool (p95 latency targets and capacity hedges)
  * Pre-agreed failover ladder (L4 -> A100 -> H100 or H100 -> A100 -> queued)
  * Capacity surge policy and billing for burst to hosted pool
  * Maintenance windows and cross-region failover notes

Happy to run a quick perf test against a representative sample if you can share an anonymized transcript sample and a small embedding batch.

—Kimberly
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Budget constraint: our target committed spend for year one is capped; can you include the 6/12/24-month pricing delta for the three pools (ballpark accepted)?
- Procurement wants a clear statement about eviction/fallback timing (e.g., how long before we get queued vs routed to A100 spare capacity).
- Can we get the 45-minute call on Thursday 10:00am PT? Anna and I will bring our procurement lead.

Next steps we expect from Redwood:
1) Finalized one-pager with the tiering matrix + conservative sizing numbers for procurement.
2) Simple SLA/failover paragraph we can paste into our RFP.
3) Pricing line items for reserved vs burst (6/12/24 month commit).

If possible please cc a contact from finance as we'll likely need an invoice path during procurement.

Thanks — Mike
